shadow:
People sort themselves into ranks. Someone is above, someone is below, and most of the time nobody decides this on purpose. It just settles, the way water finds the low ground. We hardly notice it because we have never lived inside anything else.

In a person it shows up as a pull. A voice in a room sounds like it knows where it is going, and you find yourself leaning toward it before you have weighed a single word. The pull is not stupidity. It is old. It kept small bands of people alive by letting them move as one body behind whoever seemed surest. The trouble is that surest and truest are not the same thing, and the pull cannot tell them apart.

Most people treat this as weakness, a failure of nerve, and shame themselves for following. That misses what is really going on. The leaning is a sense, and a sense can be trained. The same nerve that gets swept into someone else's current is the nerve that will one day feel exactly where your own ground stops and theirs begins. You do not kill the pull. You learn to feel it pulling, which is slower than it sounds.
repressive: Some people carry the weight to lead and never let it show. They stay back, decide they are not the type, and the unspoken thing turns sour inside them. It can ache in the body. It looks like modesty. It is closer to a held breath.
reactive: Others know they sway a room and use it. They keep people leaning on them, feed the need, frame themselves as the one with the answer. It can look like strength. Underneath it is a fear of what happens if anyone stops needing them.
gift:
Two things stop. A person quits handing their direction to whoever sounds certain, and quits gathering followers of their own. What opens on the other side is the knack for helping someone find their own next step without ever placing it for them.

That knack is guidance. Most of it is not advice. It is listening so closely that the other person hears their own thought land for the first time, and answers themselves. The old picture of the leader out front, pointing, falls away. What replaces it is quieter. You hold a kind of steady field, and inside that field someone gets clear.

Think of water under the ground. Nobody sees it. It gathers slowly, drop by drop, through seasons, and then in some unplanned spot it reaches the surface and a spring opens. People come to springs without being called. They settle there. Guidance works the same way. It is not pushed out. It collects in a person through small honest acts, year on year, until it simply rises where it is needed. And the one being guided is not made smaller by it. They walk off more themselves than before, which is the whole test of whether it was guidance at all.
siddhi:
The person is no longer the one doing this. It is what the life gives off. Virtue here has nothing to do with being good in the way a rule is good. It is the plain power of someone living straight from their own source, with nothing crooked in between.

The spring is running now. It feeds whatever is near it without choosing, the way real water does not ask who drinks. Small unseen acts, a kindness nobody clocked, an honesty that cost something, these are not stored up for credit. They just move through, and each one quietly mends a piece of the broken thing the world has been carrying.

From here the old sorting into higher and lower looks different. The ranks were never the enemy. They were people reaching, in the only shape they knew, for something to stand near and trust. That reaching was the spring trying to find its way up through stone. It always was going somewhere.
